exposure: maternal blood angiogenic factors (sFlt-1 and PlGF)
absent end-diastolic flow (AEDF) or reversed end-diastolic flow (REDF) in the umbilical artery
outcome: prolonged neonatal intensive care unit hospitalization
cohort: The study included 79 women with singleton pregnancies diagnosed with suspected-small-for-gestational-age (sSGA) fetuses between 24 and 35 6/7 weeks' gestation.
finding: Angiogenic factors testing, particularly the sFlt-1/PlGF ratio, effectively predicts critical adverse perinatal outcomes (CAPO) in sSGA pregnancies before 36 weeks' gestation and can reduce clinician judgment errors.
